findings.title: Embedded author link lightness arguments are swapped
findings.body: In .embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a, the color was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) and is now dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)). Every other conversion in this PR keeps the original percentage on the light-theme branch and uses 100 minus that percentage on $secondary for the dark branch. Here those arguments are inverted, so light themes render embedded reply author names much lighter than before (70% toward white instead of 30%), and dark themes use a 30% scale of $secondary instead of the 70% complement, leaving the names too dark on a dark background. It should be dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%)).

findings.title: Mobile flag-modal hint lightness is inverted
findings.body: .custom-message-length was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%) and is now dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%)). The light and dark branches are swapped relative to the rest of the migration. The same selector in desktop/modal.scss was converted correctly to 70% on $primary and 30% on $secondary. On mobile, light themes therefore show a much darker character-count hint than before, and dark themes get a 70% scale of $secondary (too light) instead of 30%. Swap the arguments so the light branch stays at 70%.

findings.title: Mobile topic-map heading lightness changed from 20% to 50%
findings.body: .topic-map h3 was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%) and is now dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%)). The light-theme percentage was not preserved; it was replaced with the 50% value from the h4 rule immediately below. In the same block, .number and i were correctly kept at 20% / 80%, and desktop topic-post.scss keeps this heading at 20% on $primary and 80% on $secondary. Mobile topic-map headings will be much more washed out in light themes and will not match the desktop dark-theme color. Restore 20% and 80%.

findings.title: Group member name color flattened from 30% to 50%
findings.body: .user-stream .group-member-info .name was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) and is now dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%)). The adjacent .title rule was already 50% and was converted correctly, so the name rule looks copied from it. Names lose the darker emphasis they had versus titles in light themes, and dark themes get a 50% scale of $secondary instead of the 70% complement of the original 30%. The light branch must stay at 30% and the dark branch must be scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%).

findings.title: Mobile group member name color flattened from 30% to 50%
findings.body: Mobile .user-stream .group-member-info .name was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) and is now dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%)), the same values as the following .title rule which was already 50%. This is the same mistaken copy as in desktop/user.scss: the light-theme percentage changed, so member names no longer read darker than titles, and the dark-theme color is a 50% scale of $secondary instead of the 70% complement of 30%. Restore 30% on $primary and 70% on $secondary.

findings.title: Default badge background no longer contrasts with its text
findings.body: .badge-notification sets color to $secondary (and &[href] does the same) while its background was changed from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%) to dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)). That complement formula is for muted text drawn on a $secondary surface. Here the text is $secondary, so the background must stay distinct from $secondary. In a dark theme $secondary is already the dark page background, and scaling it only 30% toward white produces a dark gray with the same dark text on top, so default count badges become unreadable. The old scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%) stayed light in dark themes because $primary is light, which is what kept the badge readable. Do not derive this background from $secondary; keep a dark-theme fill that still contrasts with $secondary text.

findings.title: Category badge count still scales only $primary
findings.body: .topic-list.categories .category .badge-notification still sets color to scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%) even though this file's other topic-list header, cell, icon, and excerpt colors were converted to dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, ...), scale-color($secondary, ...)). In dark themes that count remains a further-lightened $primary, which is the exact failure this change is meant to fix, and it will not match the muted color now used by the surrounding list text. Convert it the same way, with 50% on $primary for light themes and 50% on $secondary for dark themes.
